items.fix: Add a "Need help or another format?" section in the same place on both pages, before the form, with phone, text relay, email, postal address and a BSL contact option. State that responses can be given by phone, post, in BSL or with help, and that paper, large print, Easy Read and audio versions are available on request, with delivery times.
items.impact: Deaf BSL users, people who cannot use or struggle with a web form, and people without reliable internet are shut out and cannot ask for an adjustment from the page they are on. Help is not in a consistent place across the two versions.
items.problem: Neither page gives a phone number, email address, postal address, text relay or BSL contact. Neither says how to ask for a paper, large print, Easy Read, audio or BSL version, or how to respond by phone, post or with an advocate. The web form is the only way to take part. The only contact route is the footer link to the accessibility statement, and the simple page lacks even that.
items.where: consultation.html lines 101-131 (whole main and footer); simplified.html lines 190-210

items.fix: Split the text into one utterance per paragraph or sentence and queue them, handle onend and onerror, and show and announce through a polite live region "Reading stopped" or "Finished reading". Combine with the read-aloud controls proposed elsewhere in the review.
items.impact: Reading can stop part-way through "What we propose", before the blue badge and journey-time paragraphs, and the user may think they heard everything and respond without the facts they missed. This affects people with dyslexia, low vision, cognitive impairments or low literacy who rely on read-aloud.
items.problem: All of main is passed as one utterance. In desktop Chrome, long utterances using network voices are known to stop after about 15 seconds without any error or event. Speech can also stop or continue in the background when the tab loses focus or the mobile screen locks. The code has no onend/onerror handler, so nothing tells the user reading stopped early.

items.fix:
Add

Tell us what you think

before the form, an instruction such as "Choose one answer. Then press Send my answer.", and after the button: "We will show you a page that says we got your answer."
items.impact: Screen-reader users cannot jump to the form by heading. Users with learning disabilities or cognitive impairments are not told to choose one answer, what to do next, or whether they can change their answer later.
items.problem:
The full page has

Respond

before its form. The simple page has only

and goes straight from "Tell us what you think by 15 December." into the fieldset, with no heading, no "Choose one answer" instruction and nothing on what happens after "Send".

items.fix: Mark the radio group required and show a linked error message ("Choose an answer to the question") with an error summary at the top. Add a "Check your answers" page, say whether and how a response can be changed, put version links before the form only or keep entries when switching, and state the closing time, e.g. "until 11:59pm on Tuesday 15 December 2026".
items.impact: People with cognitive impairments, memory difficulties or tremor, screen-reader users and people switching versions send blank or unintended responses, or lose a long comment and give up. Responses cannot be taken back.
items.problem: No radio button is required and nothing checks the form before sending, so "Send my response" or "Send" can submit nothing. There is no "check your answers" step and no information on whether a response can be changed after sending. Following "Simplify this page" or "See the full page" goes to a new page and loses the answer and comments without warning. Neither page gives a closing time for 15 December.
